catalogue: Australian external decks, balconies, terraces and above-ground waterproofing

objects.name: external deck, balcony and terrace system
objects.definition: The complete weather-exposed trafficable construction outside or on top of a house, including its selected surface, supporting structure, connections, edges, drainage or open joints, waterproofing where required, and interfaces with walls, doors and barriers.
functions: Transfer people, furniture and environmental actions to the building or ground
Coordinate drainage, durability and safe edges

cad.pattern: One coordinated assembly per distinct external trafficable platform
cad.placement: Outside the envelope or over a roof, room or open subfloor
cad.opening: Drains, hatches, board gaps and service penetrations remain explicit
cad.load: Surface actions through finish, substrate or framing to supports and foundations

notes: Deck, balcony and terrace are use and topology words, not proof of one material or compliance route.

objects.name: open-jointed raised deck assembly
objects.definition: A raised trafficable surface made from spaced boards, panels or grating that lets water pass through to an open or separately drained space below, supported by exterior-suitable framing and foundations.
functions: Provide a drained outdoor walking surface
Keep surface and framing ventilated where detailed

ncc_references.relationship: Identifies spaced decking with framing suitable for external use as an exception from the H2D8(1) membrane pathway; all other applicable duties remain.

cad.pattern: Repeated surface units across a framed support grid
cad.placement: Above external ground, open space or a separate drainage construction
cad.opening: Every designed board, panel or grating joint is an actual drainage opening
cad.load: Traffic surface to joists, bearers, posts and footings

notes: Water passing through the surface must have a safe destination; open joints are not a waterproofing system.

objects.name: timber-framed external deck assembly
objects.definition: An external deck whose primary support grid is timber posts or other supports, bearers and joists, with bracing, connectors and a selected trafficable surface.
functions: Transfer deck actions through timber framing
Provide a coordinated durable framing layout
materials: naturally durable or preservative-treated structural timber

cad.pattern: Posts or supports carrying bearer lines and repeated joists
cad.placement: Below external decking
cad.start: Footings, wall support or primary bearings
cad.opening: Trimmed openings and access zones use explicit framing
cad.load: Deck actions through joists, bearers and posts to footings or building support

notes: Natural durability and preservative treatment are different evidence paths; sapwood must not inherit a heartwood durability rating.

objects.name: steel-framed external deck assembly
objects.definition: An external deck whose primary support grid uses cold-formed or structural steel posts, beams or bearers and joists, with designed connections, corrosion protection and a compatible surface system.

cad.pattern: Primary steel support lines with repeated steel joists
cad.placement: Below external decking
cad.opening: Trimmed openings and drainage paths remain explicit
cad.load: Deck actions through steel joists and beams to supports

objects.name: building-attached framed deck
objects.definition: A framed deck with at least one primary support or lateral connection taken from the building, while its outer edge is supported by posts, beams, walls or another designed support.
functions: Extend an external platform from the building
Transfer selected reactions into building structure
Coordinate the wall junction and water shedding

cad.pattern: One building-side support line and one or more outer support lines
cad.placement: Along an external building wall
cad.opening: Wall drainage and cladding clearances remain open
cad.load: Selected gravity and lateral reactions to building and external supports

notes: Part 12.3 is a limited waling-plate solution, not a general attached-deck rule; work outside its scope needs another compliant design path.

objects.name: freestanding framed deck
objects.definition: A deck supported independently on its own posts, beams, footings or other structure without relying on a building wall for primary vertical or lateral support.
functions: Provide an independently supported external platform
Avoid transferring primary deck reactions into the building
Allow a drained and inspectable building-side separation
not_synonyms: attached deck with a wall gap only

cad.pattern: Independent rows of posts and bearers beside the building
cad.placement: Near or away from a building
cad.opening: Building-side gap and access remain explicit
cad.load: All primary deck actions to its own supports and foundations

notes: Freestanding describes load path, not lack of required bracing or approval.

objects.name: low-clearance or close-to-ground deck assembly
objects.definition: A framed or supported deck with limited separation from soil, paving or a slab below, requiring deliberate drainage, ventilation, access and material selection because drying conditions are restricted.
functions: Bridge a prepared ground or slab support zone
Manage restricted airflow and splash exposure

cad.pattern: Shallow support grid close to prepared surface
cad.placement: Above ground, paving or concrete
cad.opening: Perimeter airflow, board gaps and access remain explicit
cad.load: Surface to shallow frame and distributed or discrete supports

notes: Restricted drying can make a nominally above-ground member behave more severely than an exposed, freely ventilated member.

objects.name: cantilevered framed deck assembly
objects.definition: A deck portion that projects beyond its last support line using continued joists, beams or a designed cantilever system rather than posts directly under the outer edge.
functions: Carry the projection through cantilever action
Keep backspan, restraint and edge loads explicit

cad.pattern: Continuous members projecting beyond a support line
cad.placement: At outer edge of framed deck
cad.opening: Trimmed openings do not interrupt the designed cantilever path
cad.load: Projection actions through member bending to backspan and supports

notes: A board overhang and a structural framing cantilever are different geometries.

objects.name: framed external balcony assembly
objects.definition: An elevated external platform associated with an upper storey and built from timber, cold-formed steel or structural steel framing, with a selected trafficable surface, drainage or waterproofing, wall junction and protected edge.
functions: Transfer balcony and barrier actions to supports

cad.pattern: Elevated platform connected to an upper-storey wall or independent frame
cad.placement: Outside an upper-storey room or circulation space
cad.opening: Door, drain and penetration openings are explicit
cad.load: Balcony, crowd, barrier and environmental actions to designed structure

objects.name: post-supported framed balcony
objects.definition: A framed balcony whose outer edge or full platform is carried by posts or columns continuing to foundations or another supporting structure.
functions: Support an elevated platform on discrete vertical members
Provide a clear gravity load path

cad.pattern: Elevated platform over one or more rows of posts
cad.placement: Outside upper-storey wall
cad.opening: Clear spaces between posts and access below remain explicit
cad.load: Platform to beams, posts and foundations

objects.name: cantilevered balcony assembly
objects.definition: An elevated external platform projecting from the building without primary posts at its outer edge, supported by cantilevered concrete, steel or timber members and their backspan or building connection.
functions: Transfer projection actions into the building
Coordinate thermal, waterproofing and wall interfaces

cad.pattern: Platform projecting from a restrained building support line
cad.placement: Outside upper-storey structure
cad.start: Building backspan, embedment or moment connection
cad.opening: Drains and penetrations avoid critical structure unless designed
cad.load: Balcony and barrier actions into building cantilever support

notes: Cantilever support is a structural property; visual absence of posts is not sufficient evidence of the load path.

objects.name: concrete balcony assembly
objects.definition: A cast-in-place or precast concrete balcony platform together with its bearings or continuity, falls, joints, edge, drainage, waterproofing or exception path, finish and penetrations.
functions: Provide a rigid elevated trafficable platform
Transfer balcony loads through concrete structure
Form the substrate for drainage and finishes

cad.pattern: One concrete platform with explicit supports, falls and edges
cad.placement: Outside an upper storey or over open or internal space
cad.opening: Outlets, overflows, sleeves and joints remain explicit
cad.load: Concrete platform to building structure or supports

notes: Concrete is not automatically watertight, and the H2D8 exceptions depend on the complete stated conditions.

objects.name: external waterproofed balcony or terrace assembly
objects.definition: A trafficable external platform in which a coordinated substrate, falls, membrane, terminations, joints, penetrations, outlets, overflows, protection and finish form the external above-ground waterproofing system.
functions: Prevent water entering protected spaces or construction
Collect and discharge rainwater through designed drainage

ncc_references.relationship: Provides the Deemed-to-Satisfy external-waterproofing route and its stated application and exceptions for Class 1 and 10 work.

cad.pattern: Continuous sloping waterproof field with turned-up perimeter and discrete drainage points
cad.placement: On applicable external horizontal surfaces above internal spaces or where otherwise selected
cad.end: Trafficable finish and free drainage discharge
cad.opening: Every drain, overflow, joint and penetration is explicitly sealed and coordinated
cad.load: Traffic through finish and protection to substrate; water to drainage fittings

notes: The membrane is one layer in a system. A model must not infer compliance from a blue face or a generic material label.

objects.name: trafficable roof terrace assembly
objects.definition: An occupiable external terrace built over a roof or internal space, combining the structural roof deck, external waterproofing, drainage, protected trafficable finish, edges and roof or wall penetrations.
functions: Provide occupiable space over a roof
Protect the membrane while allowing drainage and maintenance

cad.pattern: Roof-wide waterproof field with raised trafficable finish and perimeter upturns
cad.placement: Over internal building space
cad.end: Trafficable finish and parapet or edge
cad.opening: Drains, overflow paths, hatches and services remain accessible
cad.load: Occupancy and finish loads to roof structure; rainwater to roof drainage

notes: Roof deck can mean the structural roof substrate or a trafficable roof terrace; the model keeps those meanings separate.

objects.name: podium terrace assembly
objects.definition: A landscaped or paved trafficable external build-up over a podium slab or roof, with membrane, protection, drainage layers, raised or bedded finish, edges, planters and service coordination.
functions: Provide an external terrace over occupied or built space
Drain the finish and concealed waterproofing plane
Protect the membrane beneath paving and landscape elements

cad.pattern: Large waterproof slab field subdivided into paved, planted and service zones
cad.placement: Over lower building space
cad.opening: Outlets, overflow routes and access panels stay discoverable
cad.load: Finish, landscape and occupancy loads to podium structure

notes: Podium work may exceed normal house-scale scope; the object is included because the same physical layers appear in attached housing and roof terraces.

objects.name: waterproof balcony over internal space
objects.definition: A balcony directly above a room, garage or other internal building space, where failure of the external surface or junctions can admit water into occupied or enclosed construction below.
functions: Direct water to primary and overflow drainage

ncc_references.relationship: Applicable external horizontal surfaces above internal spaces are within the provision unless a stated exception applies.

cad.pattern: Waterproof field vertically aligned over internal floor area
cad.placement: Outside upper level and above internal space
cad.opening: Drain and penetration coordinates relate to the room below
cad.load: Balcony loads to structure; water excluded from internal space

objects.name: balcony over open external space
objects.definition: An elevated balcony above an open external area rather than an internal room, with its surface, structure, soffit if present, drainage, door junction and edge protection selected for exposure.
functions: Discharge water safely to an external destination

cad.pattern: Elevated platform with open external volume below
cad.placement: Outside upper storey
cad.opening: Water discharge and soffit access remain explicit
cad.load: Platform to supports; runoff to safe external discharge

notes: Open space below changes consequence and sometimes the compliance route, but does not remove the need for drainage, durability and weatherproof wall junctions.

objects.name: tiled external balcony assembly
objects.definition: A solid external balcony build-up finished with bonded tiles over a compatible bed or adhesive and external waterproofing substrate, including grout, movement joints, perimeter details, drains and thresholds.
functions: Transfer traffic through the tile build-up
Coordinate joints and drainage above the waterproofing plane

cad.pattern: Repeated tile grid following substrate falls
cad.placement: Above compatible external waterproofing build-up
cad.opening: Drains, movement joints and perimeters interrupt the tile grid
cad.load: Traffic through tiles and bed to structural substrate

notes: Tiles, grout and adhesive are not the external waterproofing membrane unless an accepted selected system says otherwise.

objects.name: pedestal-supported paver terrace assembly
objects.definition: A trafficable finish of discrete exterior pavers supported above a sloping waterproofing or hard substrate on fixed or adjustable pedestals, leaving open joints and a concealed drainage and service cavity.
functions: Create a level trafficable finish over falls
Let water pass to the drainage plane below
Keep membrane and concealed services accessible

cad.pattern: Paver grid supported at corners and supplementary points
cad.placement: Above waterproofed terrace, balcony or roof substrate
cad.opening: Open paver joints and removable drain-access zones remain explicit
cad.load: Pavers to pedestals and substrate; water through joints to drainage plane

notes: Pedestal capacity, paver strength and wind restraint are selected-system inputs; visual support at four corners is not enough evidence.

objects.name: pedestal-supported deck tile assembly
objects.definition: A raised trafficable finish of removable timber, composite, aluminium or other exterior deck panels carried directly by pedestals or by rails on pedestals over a drained substrate.
functions: Provide a removable deck-like terrace finish
Allow access to membrane, drains and services

cad.pattern: Repeated removable panels on pedestal points or support rails
cad.placement: Above protected waterproofing or drained hard substrate
cad.opening: Panel joints and inspection modules remain open or removable
cad.load: Panels through supports to structural substrate

objects.name: under-deck drainage assembly
objects.definition: A secondary system of trays, membranes, channels, gutters, flashings and outlets installed below or between open decking and its framing to collect water passing through the surface and discharge it away.
functions: Collect water passing through open decking
Create a drier usable zone below where designed
Discharge collected water without wetting vulnerable construction

cad.pattern: Repeated sloping collection bays draining to a common gutter
cad.placement: Below or between joists under open-jointed decking
cad.opening: Clean-out and overflow paths remain accessible
cad.load: Water to trays and gutter; assembly supported from framing without trapping moisture

notes: Adding a concealed water collector can reduce drying around framing; ventilation and inspectability remain deliberate.

objects.name: terrace planter waterproofing assembly
objects.definition: The planter shell, external above-ground membrane, protected upturns, root protection, drainage layer, filter fabric, outlet, overflow and soil-retaining interfaces built on a terrace, balcony or podium.
functions: Contain planting medium and irrigation water
Drain excess water while retaining soil

cad.pattern: Contained planted volume over a drained waterproof base
cad.placement: On terrace, balcony, roof or podium
cad.opening: Drain and overflow remain separate and maintainable
cad.load: Wet soil, plants and water to planter shell and supporting structure

notes: A planter can conceal membrane terminations and add large saturated loads; it is not treated as decoration only.

objects.name: deck and balcony support frame
objects.definition: The coordinated posts or other supports, bearers, joists, edge members, blocking, bracing and connections that carry a framed external deck or balcony surface.
functions: Provide fixing lines for surfaces, edges and barriers

cad.pattern: Hierarchical grid of primary and secondary members
cad.placement: Between foundations or building supports and trafficable surface
cad.opening: Openings are framed with explicit trimmers and headers
cad.load: Surface and edge actions through joists, bearers and supports

notes: Generic bearer and floor-joist objects are reused; exterior exposure and installed deck role are assembly attributes.

objects.name: deck or balcony support post
objects.definition: A vertical timber, steel or other designed member carrying a deck or balcony bearer, beam or local frame down to a footing or supporting structure.
functions: Provide a bracing and connection point
Transfer loads to the footing or structure below

cad.pattern: Repeated at bearer or beam support points
cad.placement: Between footing and deck beam or bearer
cad.opening: Keeps inspection and drainage clear around base
cad.load: Axial compression plus designed lateral and connection actions

notes: A deck support post and a barrier post have different load paths even when they align visually.

objects.name: deck-post footing assembly
objects.definition: The concrete pad, pier or other designed foundation together with reinforcement where required, embedded or surface post anchor, drainage separation and surrounding ground interface supporting one deck post.
functions: Spread post reactions into the ground
Locate and restrain the post base
Separate vulnerable post material from soil and standing water where detailed

cad.pattern: One foundation object at each supported post
cad.placement: In or on competent founding material below deck
cad.end: Post base connection above drainage surface
cad.opening: Keeps post and inspection zone clear of retained soil
cad.load: Post compression, uplift and lateral reactions to ground

notes: Footing dimensions are project design values, not defaults from a generic deck component.

objects.name: concrete deck-post pier
objects.definition: A discrete cast concrete pier or bored footing projecting to or above ground level and receiving a post anchor or, where specifically designed, an embedded post.
functions: Carry a post reaction to founding material
Raise the post connection above surrounding ground
Provide mass for uplift and lateral restraint

cad.pattern: Discrete vertical pier at post grid
cad.placement: Below each nominated deck post
cad.opening: Anchor hole or embedment remains explicit
cad.load: Post reactions into ground

objects.name: deck-post stirrup or standoff anchor
objects.definition: A galvanized, stainless or otherwise exposure-suitable metal base fitting anchored into concrete and bolted, screwed or nailed to a deck post, commonly holding timber above the wet ground or concrete surface.
functions: Locate and restrain the post base
Provide a documented standoff from wet surfaces

cad.pattern: One fitting centred at each timber post base
cad.placement: Between concrete footing and post
cad.opening: Standoff gap stays open to drain and inspect
cad.load: Post compression, uplift and shear through fitting to footing

notes: A metal standoff reduces direct wetting but does not compensate for unsuitable timber or trapped debris around the base.

objects.name: deck-post base separation pad
objects.definition: A thin durable, non-water-holding separator or bearing layer placed between a post or steel base and its support where the selected connection detail requires isolation, drainage or corrosion separation.

cad.pattern: One thin pad per nominated post or base plate
cad.placement: At post or base bearing surface
cad.opening: Does not dam water around the bearing
cad.load: Local compression only where selected

objects.name: deck bearer support line
objects.definition: A continuous or spliced line of one or more timber, cold-formed steel or structural steel bearers carrying deck joists across posts, walls or other supports.
functions: Distribute joist reactions to posts or walls

cad.pattern: Parallel primary member runs at post or wall supports
cad.placement: Below and usually across deck joists
cad.opening: Splices occur only at documented locations
cad.load: Joist reactions to posts, walls or columns

notes: Bearer and beam are overlapping trade terms; the object records support role and section rather than guessing from the word alone.

objects.name: deck joist field
objects.definition: The repeated parallel timber or steel joists, including end, rim, trimming and doubled members where required, that directly support decking or a structural balcony substrate.
functions: Transfer reactions to bearers, walls or waling plates
Define fixing lines and surface span

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel members with local doubles and trimmers
cad.placement: Between bearer or wall support lines and directly below surface
cad.opening: Trimmer assemblies frame every service or hatch opening
cad.load: Surface reactions to primary supports

objects.name: deck rim or boundary joist
objects.definition: A joist-depth member closing or defining the side or end of a deck joist field, tying joist ends together and providing selected support for fascia, surface edges or barrier backing.
functions: Close and align the joist field
Transfer selected edge and connection actions

cad.pattern: Continuous member around nominated joist-field edges
cad.placement: At joist ends or side boundary
cad.opening: Drainage and ventilation are not sealed unintentionally
cad.load: Joist-end, edge and selected barrier reactions to frame

notes: Fascia joist can refer to a structural boundary member; fascia board is normally a separate finish object.

objects.name: deck opening trimmer assembly
objects.definition: The trimming joists, headers, local doubles and connectors that frame an opening through a deck or balcony support grid for a hatch, stair, tree, drain, service or other interruption.
functions: Redirect cut-joist reactions around an opening

cad.pattern: Rectangular or shaped perimeter framing around opening
cad.placement: Within deck joist field
cad.opening: Reserved opening is the defining void
cad.load: Interrupted joist reactions through headers and trimmers to intact frame

objects.name: doubled deck-joist support
objects.definition: Two or more joists fastened or detailed to act together at a concentrated load, partition, opening, board joint, barrier fixing or other documented support line.
functions: Increase local support capacity or width
Provide a fixing zone for edges or loads
Transfer local actions into the joist field
not_synonyms: two adjacent joists with no connection

cad.pattern: Parallel connected joists at selected line
cad.placement: At opening, edge, joint or concentrated load
cad.opening: Inter-ply gaps do not become water traps
cad.load: Local load shared by connected joists

notes: Whether members truly act together depends on the designed connection; proximity alone is not composite action.

objects.name: deck cantilever-joist zone
objects.definition: The projecting portions of deck joists beyond their outer bearer or support together with their backspans, blocking, edge member and surface overhang relationship.
functions: Keep structural cantilever and board overhang separate

cad.pattern: Repeated joist ends projecting past a common support
cad.placement: At outer deck edge
cad.opening: Blocking and surface joints follow designed layout
cad.load: Projection actions through joist bending to support and backspan

objects.name: deck joist blocking row
objects.definition: A line of solid blocks, herringbone members or proprietary bridging between deck joists used to restrain rotation, align the frame or distribute selected local actions.
functions: Provide local load or fixing distribution where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated pieces between each joist along one line
cad.placement: Within deck joist depth
cad.opening: Services pass only through permitted zones
cad.load: Rotational and local distribution actions between joists

notes: Nogging is common Australian trade language here, but the canonical term retains the floor-framing function: joist blocking.

objects.name: deck barrier-post framing support assembly
objects.definition: The doubled joists, blocks, edge beam, plates, brackets and fasteners that strengthen a deck or balcony frame locally beneath a barrier post, spigot or continuous glazing channel.
functions: Distribute barrier actions into the frame
Keep waterproofing and drainage coordinated around the fixing

cad.pattern: Local reinforced framing at each barrier support
cad.placement: At open deck or balcony edge
cad.end: Multiple joists, edge beam or primary structure
cad.opening: Waterproof collar and drainage remain unblocked
cad.load: Barrier actions into deck or balcony structure

notes: A fascia board alone is not assumed capable of carrying barrier loads.

objects.name: deck or balcony edge beam
objects.definition: A primary structural member along a platform edge carrying joists, slab edge reactions, fascia and selected barrier loads between posts, walls or cantilever supports.
functions: Provide a structural line for edge and barrier connections

cad.pattern: Continuous or spliced member along supported platform edge
cad.placement: At outer or opening edge
cad.opening: Drainage outlets and penetrations are coordinated structurally
cad.load: Edge, joist, slab and barrier actions to supports

objects.name: deck concentrated-load support frame
objects.definition: Additional beams, joists, posts, footings, plates or slab thickening arranged under a heavy item such as a spa, large planter, masonry feature or equipment unit on a deck or terrace.
functions: Carry a documented concentrated or sustained load
Distribute the load to adequate supports
Keep drainage, access and waterproofing clear

cad.pattern: Local reinforced support zone under scheduled heavy item
cad.placement: Within deck, balcony or terrace structure
cad.opening: Drains and service routes remain accessible
cad.load: Concentrated load through local frame to supports

notes: Domestic deck guides commonly exclude spas and other unusually heavy loads; the object therefore carries an explicit engineered-design flag.

objects.name: deck joist hanger
objects.definition: A formed metal connector supporting and restraining the end of a deck joist against a bearer, beam, header or waling plate using the connector's specified fasteners.
functions: Support a joist end without direct bearing
Transfer joist reaction to its support
Restrain the joist at the connection

cad.pattern: One connector at each nominated supported joist end
cad.placement: Between joist end and bearer, header or waling plate
cad.opening: Every required fastener position remains available
cad.load: Joist reaction through connector and fasteners to support

notes: Capacity belongs to the selected connector, support, joist and complete fastener schedule.

objects.name: deck bearer-to-post connector
objects.definition: A bracket, saddle, cleat, notch-and-bolt detail or proprietary fitting connecting a deck bearer or beam to the top or side of a support post.
functions: Locate the bearer on the post
Transfer bearing, uplift and lateral actions

cad.pattern: One connection at each post and bearer intersection
cad.placement: At post top or side
cad.opening: Water does not become trapped in an undrained pocket
cad.load: Bearer reaction and restraint through connector to post

objects.name: deck-post cap or bearer saddle
objects.definition: A shaped metal fitting seated on top of a deck post and wrapping or cradling a bearer or beam to provide bearing, alignment and restraint.
functions: Seat the bearer over the post
Transfer uplift and lateral restraint through fasteners

cad.pattern: One formed fitting per supported post top
cad.placement: Between post top and bearer
cad.opening: Top and side geometry follows selected product
cad.load: Bearing and restraint between bearer and post

objects.name: deck framing angle bracket
objects.definition: A right-angle or folded metal bracket connecting intersecting deck members or tying framing to concrete or masonry where its selected capacity and fasteners suit the action.
functions: Transfer selected shear, uplift or restraint

cad.pattern: Discrete at nominated framing junctions
cad.placement: At intersecting members or frame-to-host interface
cad.opening: Hole pattern and edge distances are explicit
cad.load: Selected forces through bracket and fasteners

notes: A generic angle shape is not automatically a structural connector.

objects.name: deck through-bolt connection assembly
objects.definition: A bolt passing fully through connected deck members with compatible washers, nut, drilled holes and bearing zones forming one structural fastening assembly.
functions: Transfer shear, tension or combined actions
Allow the complete fastener stack to be inspected
materials: hot-dip galvanized or stainless steel bolt

cad.pattern: One or more full-depth fastener axes through connection
cad.placement: At post, bearer, beam, splice or bracing junction
cad.opening: Drilled hole is concentric and retains edge distances
cad.load: Member actions through bolt shear or tension and washer bearing

objects.name: deck framing bolt
objects.definition: A headed threaded metal fastener used with a nut and washers in an exterior deck or balcony framing connection, selected for diameter, grade, length and corrosion exposure.

cad.pattern: Discrete cylindrical fastener at scheduled connection holes
cad.placement: Through connected framing
cad.opening: Passes through aligned drilled hole
cad.load: Shear, tension and bearing in complete connection

objects.name: deck framing bolt nut
objects.definition: A threaded nut matched to a deck framing bolt and used with the required washer to clamp an exterior structural connection.

cad.pattern: One nut per through bolt
cad.placement: On threaded end outside washer
cad.opening: Threaded bore follows bolt axis
cad.load: Bolt tension through nut threads to washer

objects.name: deck framing bolt washer
objects.definition: A flat, square, round or plate washer placed beneath a deck bolt head or nut to distribute bearing and protect the connected material.

cad.pattern: At bolt head and nut where scheduled
cad.placement: Between metal fastener and connected surface
cad.end: Bolt head or nut bearing face
cad.opening: Central hole follows bolt axis
cad.load: Local bearing spread into connected material

objects.name: deck framing coach screw
objects.definition: A heavy headed screw with coarse wood thread driven into a predrilled timber member to connect deck framing or a bracket where the selected design permits.
functions: Develop withdrawal and shear resistance in timber

cad.pattern: Discrete fasteners at scheduled timber connections
cad.placement: Through first member or bracket into receiving timber
cad.opening: Predrilled hole and embedment axis remain explicit
cad.load: Shear and withdrawal through screw thread and head bearing

notes: Coach screw is not a synonym for the small corrosion-resistant screws fixing decking boards.

objects.name: proprietary deck structural screw
objects.definition: An engineered exterior screw with documented diameter, thread, head, material, coating and connection capacities used in deck framing in place of or alongside bolts, nails or coach screws.

cad.pattern: Repeated at documented structural connection
cad.placement: Through connector or member into receiving framing
cad.opening: Installation axis and edge distances are explicit
cad.load: Documented screw action into connected members

notes: The word structural is a product-evidence claim, not a visual screw shape.

objects.name: deck connector fastener group
objects.definition: The complete set and pattern of manufacturer-specified nails, screws or anchors filling the required holes of a deck hanger, bracket, strap or plate.
functions: Fix the connector to all required members
Keep fastener count and pattern explicit

cad.pattern: Fastener instance at each required connector hole
cad.placement: Through connector into framing
cad.opening: Unfilled required holes remain detectable
cad.load: Connector force through complete fastener group

notes: Substituting fastener type, length or count can change connector capacity.

objects.name: deck-frame concrete anchor
objects.definition: A cast-in, mechanical or bonded anchor connecting a deck bracket, base plate, waling alternative or support frame to concrete, selected for substrate, edge distance, exposure and actions.

cad.pattern: Discrete anchors through bracket or plate
cad.placement: At deck-frame connection to concrete
cad.opening: Drilled hole, edge distance and clearance are explicit
cad.load: Fixture actions through anchor to concrete

notes: Anchor suitability and capacity cannot be inferred from diameter alone.

objects.name: deck framing splice plate
objects.definition: A steel, timber or engineered plate spanning a joint between aligned deck framing members and fastened to each side to transfer the documented splice actions.

cad.pattern: Plate centred across framing member joint
cad.placement: At approved bearer, beam, joist or brace splice
cad.opening: Joint gap and fastener holes remain explicit
cad.load: Member actions through fasteners and plate

objects.name: deck bearer splice assembly
objects.definition: The joint between bearer segments, including support location, end preparation, overlap or butt geometry, plates, bolts or screws and moisture-shedding detail.
functions: Transfer documented actions or provide supported continuity
Keep the joint aligned and inspectable

cad.pattern: Discrete joint along bearer line
cad.placement: Over support or at engineered location
cad.opening: Joint and drainage separation remain explicit
cad.load: Bearer actions through bearing or splice connectors

objects.name: deck joist splice assembly
objects.definition: A designed joint between deck joist segments using overlap, paired members, plates or other connectors at an approved support or engineered location.

cad.pattern: Discrete splice within selected joist line
cad.placement: At support or engineered splice zone
cad.opening: Surface remains supported across splice
cad.load: Joist actions through bearing or splice connectors

objects.name: deck subframe cross-bracing assembly
objects.definition: Diagonal timber, steel angle, rod or strap members crossing between posts, bearers or beams in a vertical plane to resist deck sway and frame racking.
functions: Transfer horizontal actions toward foundations or braced structure

cad.pattern: Opposed or repeated diagonals between support points
cad.placement: In vertical planes below deck
cad.end: Upper post, bearer or beam region
cad.opening: Access and services do not interrupt the brace path
cad.load: Lateral actions through axial brace forces to supports

notes: This is vertical subframe bracing; the existing Part 12.3 strap assembly braces an attached deck in plan.

objects.name: deck post knee brace
objects.definition: A short diagonal brace between a deck post and bearer, beam or joist zone that stiffens their corner and reduces frame sway.
functions: Transfer local lateral action through axial force

cad.pattern: Short diagonal at selected post corners
cad.placement: Between post and horizontal support member
cad.opening: Maintains required access and head clearance
cad.load: Axial brace action between post and beam

objects.name: deck lateral tie assembly
objects.definition: A rod, strap, bracket or framed connection tying a deck or balcony to a suitable building or braced support to resist horizontal separation or movement without serving as the primary gravity support.
functions: Transfer lateral action to braced structure
Keep gravity and lateral support roles separate

cad.pattern: Discrete ties at designed positions
cad.placement: Between deck framing and braced building or support
cad.opening: Wall weathering remains sealed around connection
cad.load: Horizontal deck action to braced host

notes: A deck can be freestanding for gravity yet still use a specifically designed lateral tie; topology and load direction are separate axes.

objects.name: deck hold-down connector
objects.definition: A strap, bracket, rod or anchored fitting restraining uplift or overturning at a deck post, beam, joist or building connection.

cad.pattern: Discrete at uplift reaction points
cad.placement: At post bases, beam supports or critical frame connections
cad.opening: Connection remains inspectable
cad.load: Tension through connector into foundation or braced host

objects.name: deck dissimilar-material isolation layer
objects.definition: A compatible non-conductive or protective separator placed between selected metals or between metal and chemically treated timber to reduce galvanic interaction, coating damage or chemical incompatibility.

cad.pattern: Thin layer at each scheduled contact interface
cad.placement: Between incompatible framing, connector or surface materials
cad.opening: Fasteners penetrate only as detailed and water can drain
cad.load: Usually non-structural separator under local bearing

notes: Compatibility is selected-system evidence; a generic black strip is not proof of adequate isolation.

objects.name: deck steel cut-edge repair coating
objects.definition: A compatible protective coating applied to cut, drilled, welded or damaged areas of galvanized or coated steel deck framing as required by the selected steel system.

cad.pattern: Local coating patches at cut or damaged steel
cad.placement: On exposed steel substrate
cad.opening: Drain holes remain open
cad.load: Non-structural protective film

objects.name: deck timber cut-end preservative treatment
objects.definition: A compatible preservative or protective treatment applied to freshly cut, drilled, notched or machined surfaces of preservative-treated deck timber where required by the treatment system.
functions: Restore the selected treatment detail after machining
Mark vulnerable end-grain and holes for inspection

cad.pattern: Local treated face at each site cut, notch or bore
cad.placement: On machined treated-timber surfaces
cad.opening: Bolt and drain holes remain functional
cad.load: Non-structural treatment layer

notes: Cut-end treatment does not upgrade unsuitable timber to a higher hazard class or prove penetration through the full member.

objects.name: deck joist-top protection tape
objects.definition: A narrow compatible self-adhered or mechanically retained strip over the top of a deck joist or bearer to shed water away from the upper face and fastener penetrations.
functions: Reduce direct wetting of the member top
Protect fastener holes and horizontal grain
Direct water toward the sides rather than into joints
materials: butyl or compatible polymer flashing tape

cad.pattern: Continuous narrow strip along selected framing tops
cad.placement: Between deck surface and joist or bearer
cad.opening: Surface fixings penetrate at documented points
cad.load: Non-structural water-shedding strip

notes: Tape can also trap moisture if the detail blocks drying or drainage; it is a selected detail, not a universal default.

objects.name: open-jointed decking surface assembly
objects.definition: The repeated decking boards, planks, panels or grating, together with intentional gaps, end and perimeter details, fasteners or clips, border boards, edge trims and finish that form an open-draining trafficable surface.
functions: Transfer foot traffic to supporting joists or rails
Allow drainage, movement and ventilation through documented joints

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel boards or modular panels over support grid
cad.placement: Directly on joists, battens or proprietary rails
cad.opening: Side, end and perimeter gaps are explicit voids
cad.load: Traffic through each board or panel to its supports

notes: A surface tool must select a product family before applying support centres, gaps, fasteners or overhang values.

objects.name: external decking board
objects.definition: One elongated exterior trafficable board spanning across deck joists or support rails, with a selected material, profile, face, edge, end, span and fastening method.
functions: Form one repeated strip of the deck surface
Transfer load to each crossed support

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel linear units
cad.placement: Across and fixed to supporting joists or rails
cad.opening: Clear side and end gaps remain between boards
cad.load: Local bending between supports and bearing at fixings

notes: Decking is a surface product; it is not used as a bearer, joist or post unless separate structural evidence explicitly says so.

objects.name: solid timber decking board
objects.definition: A sawn or machined solid timber board selected for exterior decking, with its species, grade, heartwood or sapwood content, moisture condition, profile, durability or treatment and coating recorded.
functions: Form a natural timber trafficable surface
Accept face or concealed fixings and exterior finish

cad.pattern: Repeated boards with documented side and end joints
cad.placement: On deck joists
cad.opening: Gaps allow drainage and seasonal movement
cad.load: Board bending and fastener reactions to joists

notes: A species trade name does not by itself prove durability, grade, heartwood content or suitability for the exposure.

objects.name: solid hardwood decking board
objects.definition: A solid timber deck board manufactured from a hardwood species, with actual species, grade, heartwood and sapwood, durability and treatment evidence retained rather than assuming all hardwood is durable.
functions: Provide a dense timber traffic surface

cad.pattern: Repeated solid hardwood boards
cad.placement: On joists at product-appropriate support centres
cad.opening: Movement and drainage gaps remain explicit
cad.load: Board span and fastener reactions

notes: Hardwood is a botanical and trade grouping, not a durability rating.

objects.name: preservative-treated softwood decking board
objects.definition: A softwood decking board whose exterior suitability relies partly or wholly on a documented preservative-treatment product and hazard-class evidence.
functions: Provide a treated timber traffic surface
Resist biological hazards within the selected treatment use

cad.pattern: Repeated treated-softwood boards
cad.placement: On exterior deck joists
cad.opening: Drainage and movement gaps remain explicit
cad.load: Board span and fastener reactions

notes: Hazard class is not natural durability and is not inferred from colour.

objects.name: modified-timber decking board
objects.definition: A timber deck board whose properties have been changed by a documented thermal, chemical or impregnation process, with exterior use, structure, fixings and finish governed by selected-product evidence.
functions: Provide a modified wood traffic surface
Use a selected durability and movement system

cad.pattern: Repeated product-specific boards
cad.placement: On compatible support grid
cad.opening: Product movement gaps remain explicit
cad.load: Documented board span to supports

notes: Modified timber is a product family, not a single generic material performance.

objects.name: wood-plastic composite decking board
objects.definition: A manufactured decking board made from polymer and wood fibre or flour, solid or cellular and optionally capped, used as a non-structural traffic surface over product-compatible supports and fixings.
functions: Accommodate product-specific thermal movement and drainage

cad.pattern: Repeated manufactured boards with product-specific gaps
cad.placement: On timber, steel or approved concrete support system
cad.opening: Side and butt gaps accommodate drainage and movement
cad.load: Non-structural board bending to supports

notes: Composite is not synonymous with maintenance-free, fire-resistant, slip-resistant or structural; each is separate evidence.

objects.name: solid-profile WPC decking board
objects.definition: A wood-plastic composite board with a substantially solid cross-section rather than continuous internal cells, with its own span, fixing and movement instructions.
functions: Provide solid edge and end geometry
Accept approved face or concealed fixings

cad.pattern: Repeated solid-section composite boards
cad.placement: On approved joists or rails
cad.opening: Only external joints and any edge grooves are open
cad.load: Board span to supports

objects.name: hollow or cellular WPC decking board
objects.definition: A wood-plastic composite deck board containing continuous internal voids or cells, requiring product-specific end, drainage, fixing and span details.
functions: Provide a lightweight composite traffic surface
Manage water and debris at internal cells

cad.pattern: Repeated cellular boards with aligned internal voids
cad.placement: On approved support grid
cad.opening: Internal cells and drainage openings are explicit
cad.load: Product-specific board section to supports

notes: End caps must not create trapped water where the selected board requires drainage.

objects.name: polymer-capped composite decking board
objects.definition: A composite deck board with a distinct co-extruded or bonded protective polymer cap over part or all of its core, with exposed ends and cut edges detailed to the selected system.
functions: Provide a capped traffic and weather surface
Protect the composite core on covered faces

cad.pattern: Repeated capped boards with core visible at cut sections
cad.placement: On compatible supports
cad.opening: Joints preserve movement and drainage
cad.load: Board core carries span; cap is surface layer

notes: A cap layer is not the external waterproofing system for the platform below.

objects.name: aluminium decking board
objects.definition: An extruded or formed aluminium plank used as an exterior traffic surface, commonly with interlocking, drained or open-jointed profiles and proprietary clips, seals or end details.
functions: Provide a durable metal traffic surface
Drain through or along the proprietary profile

cad.pattern: Repeated interlocking or spaced extrusions
cad.placement: Across timber, steel or aluminium supports
cad.opening: Profile joints and drainage channels follow selected system
cad.load: Plank bending and clip reactions to supports

notes: An interlocking aluminium surface may manage water but is not automatically an AS 4654 membrane system.

objects.name: fibre-cement decking plank
objects.definition: A manufactured fibre-cement plank designed as an exterior traffic surface over specified supports and fixed, joined, sealed and finished to its product system.
functions: Provide a non-timber plank traffic surface
Receive the selected joint and coating system

cad.pattern: Repeated narrow fibre-cement planks
cad.placement: On approved joists or battens
cad.opening: Joints follow product system rather than assumed board gaps
cad.load: Plank span and fasteners to supports

notes: Product-system literature decides whether joints are open, sealed or coated.

objects.name: exterior structural fibre-cement flooring sheet
objects.definition: A structural fibre-cement floor sheet fixed across deck or balcony joists to form a continuous exterior substrate for a selected water-resistant or waterproof finish system.
functions: Form a continuous structural floor substrate
Receive sealed joints, primer, membrane or finish as selected

cad.pattern: Staggered sheet layout over joist grid
cad.placement: Directly on compatible exterior framing
cad.opening: Movement joints, drains and penetrations are trimmed and sealed
cad.load: Sheet bending and diaphragm actions to joists as documented

notes: Moisture resistance of the sheet is not the same as a complete external waterproofing system.

objects.name: open metal deck grating panel
objects.definition: A removable or fixed steel, stainless-steel or aluminium grating panel with open bars or perforations spanning between supports as an exterior traffic surface.
functions: Provide a highly drained traffic surface
Allow light, air and water through the panel

cad.pattern: Repeated grating panels with bearing bars spanning supports
cad.placement: On steel, timber or concrete ledges
cad.opening: Every grating aperture and panel joint is an opening
cad.load: Bearing bars to supports and clips

notes: Open grating can conflict with accessible routes, barefoot use or small-object control; opening geometry remains queryable.

objects.name: deck-board side gap
objects.definition: The continuous open space between the long edges of adjacent decking boards, sized for drainage, debris passage, movement, ventilation and safe use according to the selected product and application.

cad.pattern: Continuous repeated void between every adjacent board pair
cad.placement: Along decking-board edges
cad.opening: The object is the drainage opening itself
cad.load: No load-bearing role

notes: Gap dimensions are product, climate, moisture and installation inputs, not one universal Australian number.

objects.name: deck-board end or butt gap
objects.definition: The open separation between the ends of decking boards meeting along one run, allowing product movement, drainage and access to supported end fixings.
functions: Keep board ends separately supported and fixable

cad.pattern: Discrete transverse gaps at board ends
cad.placement: Over double joist, breaker board support or product-approved support
cad.opening: Gap is an explicit open joint
cad.load: No load; adjacent board ends bear independently

notes: A line of aligned butt joints may need a breaker-board or double-support detail; it is not silently permitted.

objects.name: decking perimeter clearance gap
objects.definition: The maintained separation between decking and a wall, post, column, threshold, planter, fixed kerb or other solid obstruction, allowing movement, drainage, ventilation and cleaning.

cad.pattern: Continuous or interrupted gap around fixed obstructions
cad.placement: At surface perimeter and penetrations
cad.opening: Gap remains open and cleanable
cad.load: No load-bearing role

notes: This gap can overlap a termite inspection strategy but the two concepts are not automatically identical.

objects.name: decking-board butt-joint assembly
objects.definition: Two decking-board ends, their open gap, separate supporting joist or double-support arrangement, end fixings and any product-specific seal, cap or coating at one surface joint.
functions: Terminate and restart a board run
Allow movement and drainage at the joint

cad.pattern: Discrete board-end pair over support
cad.placement: At board length break
cad.opening: Butt gap remains open
cad.load: Each board end transfers independently to support

objects.name: staggered decking butt-joint layout
objects.definition: A board layout in which end joints occur on different support lines rather than forming one continuous seam, while every end remains independently supported and fixed.
functions: Distribute visible and local joint lines
Coordinate stock lengths and support positions

cad.pattern: End joints offset across successive board rows
cad.placement: Across full deck surface
cad.opening: Each butt gap remains explicit
cad.load: Each board spans independently between supports

objects.name: decking breaker board
objects.definition: A deck board installed across or at an angle to the main board direction to interrupt long runs, separate fields, receive aligned board ends or accommodate movement and stock lengths.
functions: Provide a deliberate line beside supported board ends
Resolve changes in direction or long runs

cad.pattern: Single or repeated transverse board line
cad.placement: Between main decking fields
cad.opening: Parallel end gaps occur on each side
cad.load: Board to its dedicated supports

notes: A breaker board requires support appropriate to its changed span direction.

objects.name: deck picture-frame border assembly
objects.definition: One or more decking boards following the perimeter of a deck and framing the ends or sides of the main board field, with dedicated support, corner joints, gaps and fixings.
functions: Finish and visually frame the deck perimeter
Cover or align main board ends

cad.pattern: Continuous board border around selected deck edges
cad.placement: At trafficable surface perimeter
cad.opening: Field-to-border gaps and corner joints are explicit
cad.load: Border boards to dedicated edge supports

objects.name: deck starter or finisher board
objects.definition: The first or last board in a decking field, often square-edged or face-fixed where a normal concealed clip cannot be installed at the perimeter.
functions: Start or terminate a board field
Close the surface layout at an edge

cad.pattern: One board row at each field edge
cad.placement: At start or finish of decking run
cad.opening: Perimeter clearance remains open
cad.load: Board to edge supports

objects.name: deck edge fascia board
objects.definition: A non-primary finish board fixed vertically to the outside face of a deck rim joist, edge beam or surface edge to conceal framing and finish the perimeter.
functions: Receive edge trims or surface returns where detailed

cad.pattern: Continuous or jointed vertical board along deck edge
cad.placement: Outside rim joist or edge support
cad.opening: Ventilation and drainage behind fascia remain explicit
cad.load: Self-weight and minor finish actions to edge framing

notes: Do not anchor barriers to fascia unless the documented structural backing and connection are modelled separately.

objects.name: decking edge trim
objects.definition: A proprietary metal, polymer or matching composite profile covering or finishing an exposed decking edge, board groove, sheet edge or transition without serving as the structural rim member.
functions: Cover a groove, cut or fixing line

cad.pattern: Continuous profile along selected exposed edge
cad.placement: At outer board, sheet or panel edge
cad.opening: Drainage slots remain open
cad.load: Finish component with minor traffic contact only

objects.name: decking-board end cap
objects.definition: A proprietary plug or closure fitted to an exposed end of a hollow, cellular or shaped decking board to finish the opening while preserving any required drainage and movement.
functions: Close or finish an exposed board end
Maintain the product's required drainage path

cad.pattern: One cap at each selected exposed cellular-board end
cad.placement: In or over board end
cad.opening: Required drain or vent holes remain open
cad.load: Non-structural retained fitting

objects.name: hollow decking drainage or vent plug
objects.definition: A shaped insert at a hollow decking-board end that limits debris or pests while permitting water or air movement required by the selected product.

cad.pattern: One vented insert at selected open cells
cad.placement: At hollow board end
cad.opening: Perforations are functional openings
cad.load: No structural role

objects.name: decking face-fixing screw
objects.definition: A corrosion-suitable screw driven through the exposed face of a decking board into timber or steel support, with product-specific head, clearance hole, countersink, edge distance and driving depth.
functions: Fix the board to its support

cad.pattern: Repeated at each board-to-support intersection
cad.placement: Through board face into joist or rail
cad.start: Head flush or at selected depth
cad.opening: Predrilled clearance and countersink follow product
cad.load: Board restraint through screw to support

notes: Overdriving can damage the surface or prevent intended movement; installed head depth is model data.

objects.name: decking face-fixing nail
objects.definition: A corrosion-suitable nail with a head and shank selected for fixing an approved timber or composite decking product to timber framing.
functions: Fix the board to timber support
Provide a visible or near-flush face fixing

cad.pattern: Repeated at board and timber-joist crossings
cad.placement: Through decking face into timber support
cad.opening: Predrilled hole where required
cad.load: Board uplift and local shear to timber support

objects.name: concealed decking clip
objects.definition: A proprietary clip engaging side grooves or the underside of adjacent decking boards and fixed to the support to hold the boards while establishing the selected side gap.
functions: Fix boards without exposed face heads

cad.pattern: One or more clips at every board-to-support crossing
cad.placement: Between grooved board edges over support
cad.end: Adjacent board groove and support screw
cad.opening: Clip establishes an open side gap
cad.load: Board restraint through clip and screw to support

notes: Clips are product systems; similar shape does not establish compatibility.

objects.name: decking starter or edge clip
objects.definition: A proprietary one-sided clip securing the first or last grooved decking board where a normal two-sided concealed clip cannot be inserted.
functions: Start or finish a concealed-fixing field

cad.pattern: Repeated along first or last board support line
cad.placement: At decking field perimeter
cad.opening: Perimeter clearance remains open
cad.load: Perimeter board restraint to support

objects.name: decking-clip fixing screw
objects.definition: The product-compatible screw fixing a concealed or starter decking clip into timber, steel or proprietary support framing.
functions: Fix the clip to the support
Allow the clip system to be installed at controlled depth

cad.pattern: One screw per clip or as product specifies
cad.placement: Through clip into support
cad.opening: Clip hole follows product geometry
cad.load: Clip restraint through screw

objects.name: decking face-screw plug
objects.definition: A matching timber, composite or polymer plug inserted over a recessed face-fixing screw to conceal the head while retaining the repair and removal strategy.
functions: Limit debris and water in the recess

cad.pattern: One plug over each selected recessed screw
cad.placement: In board face counterbore
cad.opening: Closes the counterbore only
cad.load: Minor foot contact; no structural connection role

objects.name: deck-board fixing adhesive
objects.definition: A product-approved exterior adhesive bead used with a concealed clip, batten, rail or other specified fixing system rather than assumed as a universal substitute for mechanical fastening.
functions: Limit movement or rattle where specified
materials: exterior polyurethane or MS polymer adhesive

cad.pattern: Continuous or intermittent bead at selected support line
cad.placement: Between board and compatible support or clip
cad.opening: Does not dam required drainage
cad.load: Supplementary bond only as selected system documents

notes: Adhesive must not be inferred or used to replace required mechanical fixings.

objects.name: decking anti-rattle or bearing pad
objects.definition: A thin resilient strip or pad between a metal or modular decking element and its support to limit noise, abrasion or minor rocking while preserving drainage and the designed fastening.

cad.pattern: Strip or discrete pads at bearings
cad.placement: Between deck element and support
cad.opening: Does not block drains or ventilation
cad.load: Local compressed bearing interface

objects.name: deck slip-resistant insert
objects.definition: A proprietary abrasive, elastomeric or profiled strip fitted into a decking groove or routed recess to alter surface traction at selected paths, steps or ramps.
functions: Mark a selected path or edge

cad.pattern: Repeated strips on selected boards or along path
cad.placement: Flush or slightly proud in traffic face
cad.opening: Recess follows board without cutting structural support
cad.load: Direct foot contact to board

notes: Slip resistance is verified for the installed surface condition, not guaranteed by drawing an insert.

objects.name: removable decking board
objects.definition: A normal or purpose-made decking board fixed with a reversible method and identified for removal to inspect or service framing, drains, valves, services or the ground below.
functions: Allow local replacement without dismantling a large field

cad.pattern: One or more identified boards above service zone
cad.placement: Within decking field
cad.opening: Removal reveals the maintenance opening
cad.load: Normal traffic when closed; removable for service

objects.name: deck inspection hatch assembly
objects.definition: A framed opening in a deck surface with a removable or hinged trafficable cover, edge support, lifting hardware and secure closure providing access below.
functions: Provide maintained access below the platform
Close the opening safely during use
Support the cover around its perimeter

cad.pattern: One framed cover module at access location
cad.placement: Within deck or raised-finish field
cad.opening: Clear maintenance opening exists when cover is removed
cad.load: Cover traffic loads to perimeter frame

objects.name: exterior timber deck finish system
objects.definition: The preparation, compatible preservative treatment where required, penetrating oil, stain, film coating or other selected exterior finish applied to timber deck boards and maintained as a documented system.

cad.pattern: Continuous finish on exposed board faces and detailed edges
cad.placement: On solid timber decking
cad.opening: Board gaps and drainage remain open
cad.load: Non-structural surface layer under traffic

notes: Oil, stain, film finish and preservative treatment are different material roles.

objects.name: external waterproofing substrate assembly
objects.definition: The structural deck or floor and any compatible topping, screed, sheeting, joints, fixings and preparation forming the stable sloping surface that receives an external above-ground membrane system.
functions: Support the membrane and trafficable build-up
Provide designed falls and junction geometry
Carry movement, drains and penetrations in a coordinated base

cad.pattern: Continuous prepared sloping field with detailed edges and openings
cad.placement: Below external membrane
cad.opening: Drains, joints and penetrations are formed before membrane
cad.load: Trafficable build-up to structural frame or slab

notes: Falls belong to substrate geometry unless the selected system explicitly forms them elsewhere; the membrane should not be drawn as the fall-forming object by default.

objects.name: concrete external-waterproofing substrate
objects.definition: A cast-in-place or precast concrete slab, topping or panel surface prepared with the required falls, curing, crack and joint treatment, edge geometry and outlet recesses to receive an external membrane.
functions: Carry the terrace or balcony build-up
Form falls, upstands and drain recesses

cad.pattern: Continuous concrete field with joint and drainage geometry
cad.placement: Below primer and membrane
cad.opening: Outlets, sleeves and joints remain explicit
cad.load: Waterproof build-up and traffic to concrete structure

notes: Concrete surface appearance is not evidence that cracks, joints, curing or moisture are suitable for the selected membrane.

objects.name: fibre-cement external-waterproofing substrate
objects.definition: A structural exterior fibre-cement sheet floor including compatible framing, tongue-and-groove or butt joints, movement joints, adhesive, fixings, sealant and primers prepared to receive the selected membrane or finish.
functions: Provide a sheet membrane substrate over framing
Coordinate sheet joints and movement below waterproofing

cad.pattern: Staggered supported sheets with explicit sealed and movement joints
cad.placement: On exterior deck or balcony framing
cad.opening: Drains and penetrations use trimmed and sealed openings
cad.load: Sheet to joists and framing

notes: Moisture resistance of a proprietary sheet does not replace the applicable external-waterproofing design.

objects.name: plywood external-waterproofing substrate
objects.definition: A structural plywood deck substrate used only where the selected membrane and complete system accept it, with sheet grade, treatment, support, joints, fixings, falls, edge sealing and moisture conditions documented.

cad.pattern: Supported staggered structural sheets
cad.placement: On exterior framing where accepted by selected system
cad.opening: Penetrations and joints receive compatible treatment
cad.load: Sheet to supporting joists

notes: This is not a universal deemed solution. Selected membrane, plywood, support and regulatory evidence must agree.

objects.name: metal external-waterproofing substrate
objects.definition: A steel or aluminium plate, pan or formed deck surface accepted by a selected external membrane system and prepared with compatible joints, fasteners, movement, primers and corrosion protection.
functions: Coordinate metal movement and corrosion with waterproofing

cad.pattern: Continuous or seamed metal deck field
cad.placement: Below external membrane where selected system permits
cad.opening: Seams, fasteners and penetrations are treated explicitly
cad.load: Membrane and traffic build-up through metal to supports

objects.name: external fall-forming screed
objects.definition: A bonded, unbonded or proprietary cementitious or resin-modified layer shaped over a structural substrate to create drainage falls and local drain or threshold geometry before the external membrane or finish.

cad.pattern: Variable-thickness layer falling from high lines to drains
cad.placement: Above structural substrate and below membrane unless selected otherwise
cad.opening: Drain bodies and joints interrupt screed
cad.load: Finish loads in compression to substrate

notes: The tool should store both structural level and finished screed surface so falls are measurable.

objects.name: external tile mortar bed
objects.definition: A cementitious bed supporting external tiles or pavers above the waterproofing or protection layer as permitted by the selected system, with falls, reinforcement, joints and drainage behaviour documented.
functions: Support a bonded tile or paver finish

cad.pattern: Continuous bed beneath tile field
cad.placement: Above protected membrane or accepted substrate
cad.opening: Drains and movement joints remain clear
cad.load: Tile traffic loads to substrate

objects.name: external waterproofing membrane primer
objects.definition: A thin product-specific preparation coat applied to the external substrate to promote membrane adhesion, control porosity or prepare a particular surface.

cad.pattern: Continuous thin coat over prepared membrane-receiving area
cad.placement: Between substrate and membrane
cad.opening: Drains and moving joints treated to system detail
cad.load: Non-structural adhesion-promoting layer

notes: Primer is selected with the membrane and substrate; it is not a generic paint material.

objects.name: external above-ground waterproofing membrane
objects.definition: The continuous liquid-applied or sheet barrier within an external above-ground waterproofing system, extended through fields, upturns, joints, drains, penetrations and terminations using compatible system components.
functions: Bridge the waterproof field and interfaces
Direct water to outlets and free edges

ncc_references.relationship: Calls up AS 4654.1 for membrane materials and AS 4654.2 for applicable external system design and installation.

cad.pattern: Continuous sealed field connected to every compatible flashing and drain
cad.placement: Above prepared substrate and below protection or exposed finish
cad.end: Drain flange, overflow or free-edge termination
cad.opening: Penetrations are sealed by collars, boots or flashings rather than holes in the barrier
cad.load: Non-structural barrier protected from traffic unless designed as exposed finish

notes: A generic membrane face carries no conformity claim until product, system, substrate and installation evidence are attached.

objects.name: liquid-applied external waterproofing membrane
objects.definition: A site-applied liquid membrane that cures to a continuous external barrier, built in the specified coats and thickness with reinforcement, bond breakers and detail materials where required.
materials: polyurethane, acrylic, cementitious-polymer or other AS 4654.1-conforming selected product

cad.pattern: Continuous coated field with reinforced details
cad.placement: On primed compatible external substrate
cad.opening: Collars and seal details preserve continuity at penetrations
cad.load: Barrier film with no assumed structural span

objects.name: sheet-applied external waterproofing membrane
objects.definition: A factory-manufactured flexible sheet laid in joined runs over an external substrate and sealed at laps, seams, corners, drains, penetrations and terminations as one waterproof barrier.
functions: Bridge the substrate with joined sheets
Connect to flashings and drainage fittings
materials: PVC or other accepted sheet system

cad.pattern: Overlapping or welded sheet runs across field
cad.placement: On compatible prepared substrate
cad.end: Final sealed sheet edge or drain
cad.opening: Seams and penetrations use explicit sealed geometry
cad.load: Barrier sheet supported by substrate

objects.name: bituminous external sheet membrane
objects.definition: A reinforced or unreinforced bitumen-based sheet membrane, torch-applied, self-adhered or otherwise installed as its selected external waterproofing system.
functions: Form a robust sheet waterproof barrier
Turn into compatible drains and flashings

cad.pattern: Lapped sheet runs with sealed seams
cad.placement: On compatible external substrate
cad.opening: Penetrations use preformed or site-fabricated collars
cad.load: Supported barrier sheet

notes: Torch application is a work method for selected products, not part of the installed object's canonical identity.

objects.name: synthetic-rubber external sheet membrane
objects.definition: An EPDM, butyl or other selected elastomeric sheet used as an external waterproof barrier with compatible seams, adhesives, tapes, flashings and terminations.
functions: Seal to compatible drains and interfaces

cad.pattern: Large flexible sheets with sealed seams and patches
cad.placement: On compatible substrate or separation layer
cad.opening: Boots and collars maintain sealed penetrations
cad.load: Flexible barrier supported by substrate

objects.name: thermoplastic external sheet membrane
objects.definition: A PVC, TPO or other selected thermoplastic waterproof sheet joined by compatible welded or bonded seams and detailed to external drains, upturns and penetrations.

cad.pattern: Sheet runs with welded or bonded seam lines
cad.placement: On compatible substrate
cad.opening: Penetrations use compatible formed or welded accessories
cad.load: Sheet supported by substrate

objects.name: external sheet-membrane adhesive
objects.definition: A product-specific full-spread, strip or contact adhesive bonding an external sheet membrane, seam, flashing or accessory to a compatible substrate or to another sheet.

cad.pattern: Continuous or specified patterned layer beneath sheet
cad.placement: Between sheet membrane and substrate or within lap
cad.opening: Does not obstruct drains or designed unbonded movement zones
